chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ahmad ibn Ashim, from al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He said: I said to him: I am your ransom, why did the Arabs name their sons with 'Kalb' (Dog), 'Nimr' (Leopard), 'Fahd' (Leopard/Panther), and similar names? He said: The Arabs were people of war, and they would intimidate the enemy with the names of their sons. They would name their slaves 'Faraj' (Relief), 'Mubarak' (Blessed), 'Maimun' (Lucky), and similar names, using them as omens of good fortune.
ai.seo_question: Why did ancient Arabs name their children after animals?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates that pre-Islamic Arabs utilized fierce animal names like 'Dog' or 'Leopard' for their free sons to instill fear in enemies during warfare, reflecting a culture of martial intimidation. Conversely, they bestowed auspicious names such as 'Furaja' (Freedom) or 'Mubarak' (Blessed) upon slaves, viewing them as omens of good fortune and liberation. This distinction highlights the socio-linguistic practices of the Jahiliyyah era, where nomenclature served specific psychological and social functions within the tribal hierarchy.
